message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most acclaimed and popular crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have been praised for their storytelling, performances, and suspenseful pacing.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Release (US) | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | May 1 | A modern psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑thriller elements, featuring a strong female lead and inventive use of technology as a weapon. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | May 15 | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced, witty style shines in this gangster caper, with a star‑packed ensemble and clever twists. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | June 12 | Though more courtroom drama, its investigative narrative and tense confrontations fit the crime‑thriller mold, earning an Oscar nomination for Best Picture. |
| 4 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | December 25 | A sprawling mob saga that uses de-aging tech to weave a long‑term crime narrative, praised for its depth and historical scope. |
| 5 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | August 28 | A Danish thriller that follows a man wrongfully accused of a crime, exploring themes of paranoia and social media hysteria. |
| 6 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | September 18 | A gritty revenge story set in colonial Australia, blending crime‑thriller tension with a strong female perspective. |
| 7 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | October 23 | A historical crime‑thriller that dramatizes a medieval duel, noted for its intense character dynamics and moral ambiguity. |
| 8 | **The Woman in the Window** | Andrew Dominik | Amy Adams, John Krasinski | November 20 | A psychological thriller with a crime‑driven plot, featuring a protagonist who becomes entangled in a possible murder investigation. |
| 9 | **The Invisible Man** (UK) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | May 1 | A psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑thriller elements, featuring a strong female lead and inventive use of technology as a weapon. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** (US) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | May 1 | A psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑thriller elements, featuring a strong female lead and inventive use of technology as a weapon. |

> **Note:** Some titles appear twice because they were released in both the UK and US on the same date; the table lists them once for clarity.

These films represent a mix of mainstream blockbusters and critically acclaimed indie projects, offering a broad view of the crime‑thriller landscape in 2020. Enjoy your viewing!
